observations: Files I read: the request JSON (with its first reading), source/original.txt and REVISION-2026-11-11.md (Request 3 and the consent follow-up). I opened these images with Read and looked at them myself, in this order: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png, then workflow/storyboards/page-05.png, then workflow/review/page-04.png, review/page-05.png and review/page-06.png. For the outgoing boundary I also viewed storyboards-unnumbered/page-06.png. I did not render the SVGs, and I did not open the character sheets.

The script matches the source exactly. The opening greeting comes first. The user-requested consent exchange ('May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?' / 'Yes, I agree.') comes before 'I've been feeling tired lately.', which answers 'Tell me what brings you in.' The label wording follows the user's full lists, as decided in the 'add page if needed' follow-up.

In the numbered storyboard, the beat notes for 05-3 and 05-4 are partly hidden or run past the panel edge. These guide notes do not appear in the unnumbered PNG or the preview, so this is not reader-facing.

Unnumbered page-05.png: in Panel A, Ananya's balloon (top centre) is the first text the eye meets; the large PATIENT DETAILS label then sits lower left. In Panel B, three boxes run left to right along the top: Ananya's question, Ravi's 'Yes, I agree.' and the consent label. In Panel C, Ravi's balloon (top left) comes before the SOAP label (lower left). Panel D has one caption. This matches the intended order.

First-reader point: 'Tell me what brings you in' is answered only after the consent exchange, and 'Yes, I agree.' might be taken as the answer to it. 'Yes, I agree.' touches the yes/no consent question in the same panel and cannot answer an open 'what brings you in' question. The consent label beside it states the context, and the laptop in the art shows a mic-and-shield consent card. Panel C's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' then clearly answers the greeting. A doctor pausing for consent before notes is natural, and it matches the user's request. Acceptable.

First-reader point: the Panel B balloons touch. This also happens in review/page-05.png. The tails split clearly, one going left-down to Ananya and the other right-down to Ravi, so the touching reads as a quick exchange, not one speaker. First-reader point: Ravi's long tail falls short of the ravi box. In the art, the tip at about (665, 745) is just above and left of Ravi's head, and he is the only figure on that side, with his open hand gesturing in agreement. Acceptable.

First-reader point: the AI VOICE CONSENT label is flush with the right border and has no full stop. It is also flush in the preview, but the text has inner margins and is not clipped. The PATIENT DETAILS and SOAP NOTES labels also have no closing full stop, so this is consistent label style. First-reader point: the dense labels crowd the art. In the art, the labels cover only the laptop screens they describe, and the SOAP panel still shows the mic icon, while faces and hands stay clear. The wording is the user's chosen full wording. Acceptable.

First-reader point: Ravi is only a dot in Panel D, and Ananya gives no verbal reply. In the art, Ravi is an over-the-shoulder back-of-head view at right, which correctly has no face box, and Ananya is attentive and listening, looking at him rather than the screen. The caption takes her turn, and her spoken reply opens 06-2 ('We'll go through your concerns...'). Acceptable.

transitions.observation: The tablet alert leads to the consultation. Ravi is seated opposite Ananya, the laptop she had closed is now open showing patient details, and the tablet is out of sight, as the section notes require.
Same seating, wider shot. The laptop shows the consent card before any listening, so the AI is not shown recording before Ravi agrees, and the mic toggle stayed off in 05-1.
After consent, Ravi describes his concern while the laptop shows the SOAP section with the mic glowing. The sequence of consent first, then listening, is visible.
Reverse angle over Ravi's shoulder onto Ananya listening. The laptop beside her shows a small mic waveform, which supports the caption that the technology is in the background.

Same consultation continues. 06-1 is a close-up of the same laptop, with Ananya's white-coat cuff and hand on the trackpad, now on the treatment-planner screen. 06-2 brings back both seated figures and her reply about next steps. I inspected review/page-06.png and storyboards-unnumbered/page-06.png for this check.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading's order was Ananya, PATIENT DETAILS, Ananya, Ravi, AI VOICE CONSENT, Ravi, SOAP NOTES, caption. That matches the intended [1,2], [1,2,3], [1,2], [1], and so does my scan. The first reader raised the delayed answer, the touching balloons, the short tail, the flush label without a full stop, the dense labels, Ravi as a dot and Ananya's silent turn. I judged each one above against review/page-05.png and page 06: none produces a skip or a mistaken reply in the accepted page. 'Yes, I agree.' is anchored to the consent question by adjacency, by meaning and by the consent card on the laptop, and the opening question is answered in 05-3.
